messages:
inc-bot: PAGER: SRE-P1 - router.fallback.loop detected in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. 70% request reroutes, error spike. Pager details: https://incidents/redwood/2450123456
alex: saw the alert, joining. oncall handoff in 5m? I'm @alex.
maya: i'm oncall, stepped in — looking at router metrics now.
jordan: grabbing customer-impact. which customers are affected?
maya: some long-tail customers on Dedicated pools hitting 502s. early sig shows traffic being blackholed to quant-variant-01 and then to fallback-region, which then bounces back due to policy misconfig.
samir: can you paste the router policy for that customer? suspect the fallback priority list contains itself (us-west-2) causing loop.
maya: pulling config: ```router.policy {
  primary: variant-stable
  fallback_chain: [quant-variant-01, us-west-2-fallback, eu-central-1]
  loop_detect: disabled
  max_hops: 10
}```
lia: whoa loop_detect disabled — that's the problem. why was that toggled?
alex: recall a perf test last week temporarily disabled loop detection for latency experiments. should be reverted asap.
jordan: customer impact list: ``customer-42, acme-ml, partner-x`` seeing increased 5xx and elevated p50/p95. Not a global outage but multiple Dedicated pools reporting heavy request drops.
maya: also seeing autoscaler churn in the Dedicated pools — the autoscaler in us-west-2 is seeing a phantom low-util signal and scaling down, which causes capacity blackholing when router routes to a drained pool. logs: ```autoscaler: pool:dedicated-usw2: scale_down(reason=heartbeat_mismatch, diff=-3)```
samir: heartbeat_mismatch? That's the metric misread we've seen before when the pool proxy answered stale stats. Which version of pool-agent is running?
maya: pool-agent v2.1.9 on those nodes. there's a known bug where proxy drops metrics during brief NVMe saturation causing a negative health flip.
lia: immediate mitigation steps?
alex: Step 1: force-enable loop detection globally on routers. Command: ```/ops router set global.loop_detect=true``` — can someone run that?
jordan: running now. ```ops-bot: running /ops router set global.loop_detect=true -> success (applied to us-west-2, eu-central-1)```
inc-bot: NOTE: automated rollback policy triggered for last router policy change at 2450122100.
maya: Step 2: put affected Dedicated pools into manual-drain-protect mode so autoscaler won't scale them down. ```/ops pool set dedicated-usw2 protected=true```
samir: I'll patch the pool-agent to 2.1.10 with the metrics fix, but that's a longer deploy. For immediate patching, we can flip the metrics source to the control-plane aggregated counter: ```/ops pool metrics-source set dedicated-usw2=controlplane```
lia: who will own customer comms? Jordan?
jordan: I can draft an initial status update: short blurb, impact (partial request failures for select Dedicated customers), mitigation steps being applied, ETA unknown.
alex: Also add a note about workaround: manual scaling protections and router loop-detection re-enabled. Avoid promising ETA.
maya: After loop_detect toggle, I'm seeing fallback hop counts drop and error rate on routers decreasing. p95 latency back to normal for many routes.
samir: autoscaler still trying to scale down older nodes. I've disabled autoscaler for the affected pool temporarily: ```/ops autoscaler pause dedicated-usw2``` — paused.
lia: lia here taking notes, will prepare post-incident doc. please add any decision bullets to thread.
jordan: posted initial status update to customers and support channels.
inc-bot: INCIDENT: Severity P1 -> Active. Assigned to oncall-maya.
alex: can we also check smart-routing policies that prefer quant variants by score? might want to lower quant-variant-01 weight temporarily.
maya: lowering variant weight: ```/ops routing weight set quant-variant-01=0.2``` -> applied.
samir: verifying traffic flow: logs show reroutes reduced and no more circular hops. pool utilization rising back to normal once autoscaler paused.
jordan: support reports ack from Acme that retries are succeeding now. Good sign.
lia: timeline note: root cause seems twofold: (1) router loop detection disabled during a perf experiment, (2) pool-agent metrics bug causing false low-util signals to autoscaler. Combined, created blackhole when router fallback chain sent traffic to drained pools causing bounce back.
alex: next steps: - revert the perf experiment flag (already done), - roll pool-agent fix in a canary then global, - add automated test that catches loop_detect=false in prod, - add a guard in autoscaler to ignore heartbeat_mismatch spikes shorter than 30s.
maya: agreed. I'll create a JIRA for pool-agent rollout and autoscaler guard.
samir: I'll run a canary deploy of pool-agent v2.1.10 to two non-prod pools and monitor metrics.
inc-bot: REMINDER: schedule postmortem meeting within 48 hours.
jordan: handoff: my shift ends in 20m, leaving this with alex as owner if anything regresses. alex?
alex: I'll watch the dashboards for another hour, then lia can pick up for next doc.
lia: lgtm. saving conversation to incident doc.
ops-bot: deploy reminder scheduled: pool-agent canary at 2450127200.
maya: closing note: monitor also for other regions — loop detection toggles might have been propagated during the experiment. searching for other routers with loop_detect=false.
alex: thanks everyone. good fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
